items.followUp: Describe the structure of the cell wall and state two of its functions.

rubric.why: Identifies the membrane as a thin, flexible boundary around the cell.
rubric.description: The cell membrane is a thin, flexible boundary surrounding the cell.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing its position and general structure.

rubric.why: Describes the membrane’s main components.
rubric.description: It consists mainly of a phospholipid bilayer with proteins embedded in it.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the phospholipid bilayer and embedded proteins.

rubric.why: States the membrane’s key property that allows controlled exchange.
rubric.description: The membrane is selectively permeable.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying selective permeability.

rubric.why: Explains the membrane’s control of exchange across it.
rubric.description: It controls the movement of substances into and out of the cell.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that it controls movement into and out of the cell.

rubric.why: States the separating function of the membrane.
rubric.description: It separates the cell contents from the external environment.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the separating function.

modelAnswer: The cell membrane is a thin, flexible boundary surrounding the cell.
It is made mainly of a phospholipid bilayer with proteins embedded in it.
It is selectively permeable.
It controls the movement of substances into and out of the cell.
It separates the cell contents from the external environment.

items.followUp: What is an enzyme? Explain how temperature can affect its activity.

rubric.why: Identifies enzymes as biological catalysts.
rubric.description: Enzymes are biological catalysts.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for defining enzymes as biological catalysts.

rubric.why: States the effect enzymes have on reactions.
rubric.description: They speed up biochemical reactions.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that they speed up biochemical reactions.

rubric.why: Recognises enzyme specificity.
rubric.description: Each enzyme is specific to a particular substrate or reaction.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that enzymes are specific.

rubric.why: Gives a further characteristic of enzymes.
rubric.description: Enzymes are not used up in reactions, and their activity depends on conditions such as temperature and pH; high temperature can denature them.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a valid additional characteristic, such as not being used up or having optimum conditions.

modelAnswer: Enzymes are biological catalysts that speed up biochemical reactions.
Each enzyme is specific to a particular substrate or reaction.
Enzymes are not used up in the reactions they catalyse.
Each enzyme works best at an optimum temperature and pH; high temperature can denature it.

items.followUp: Define anaerobic respiration and describe one industrial use of it.

rubric.why: Defines fermentation as the breakdown of glucose in the absence of oxygen.
rubric.description: Fermentation is the anaerobic breakdown of glucose by microorganisms or their enzymes.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the anaerobic breakdown and 1 mark for identifying glucose as the substance broken down.

rubric.why: Names the products of yeast fermentation.
rubric.description: In yeast, fermentation produces ethanol and carbon dioxide.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming both products.

rubric.why: Gives bread making as an important use of fermentation and explains its effect.
rubric.description: Fermentation is used in bread making; carbon dioxide makes the dough rise.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for bread making and the role of carbon dioxide.

rubric.why: Gives another useful application of fermentation.
rubric.description: Fermentation is also used to produce alcoholic beverages.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that fermentation is used to produce alcoholic beverages.

modelAnswer: Fermentation is the anaerobic breakdown of glucose by microorganisms or their enzymes.
In yeast, fermentation produces ethanol and carbon dioxide and releases a small amount of energy.
Fermentation is used in bread making; carbon dioxide makes the dough rise.
It is also used to produce alcoholic beverages.
Fermentation is important in making useful food and industrial products.

items.followUp: State how nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium in fertilizers help crops grow.

rubric.why: States that fertilizers supply nutrients needed by plants.
rubric.description: Fertilizers supply essential mineral nutrients to plants.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that fertilizers supply essential plant nutrients.

rubric.why: Names the main nutrients commonly supplied by fertilizers.
rubric.description: They commonly provide nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium.

rubric.why: Explains how fertilizers restore or improve soil nutrient levels.
rubric.description: They replenish nutrients in the soil and improve its fertility.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for replenishing soil nutrients or improving soil fertility.

rubric.why: Connects fertilizer use with improved crop growth or production.
rubric.description: This promotes plant growth and increases crop yield.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for improved growth or crop yield.

modelAnswer: Fertilizers supply essential mineral nutrients to plants.
They commonly provide nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium.
They replenish nutrients in the soil and improve its fertility.
This promotes plant growth and increases crop yield.

items.followUp: Compare the structure of arteries and veins and state the direction in which each carries blood.

rubric.why: States the direction of blood flow in arteries.
rubric.description: Arteries carry blood away from the heart to the body organs.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct direction of blood flow.

rubric.why: Describes the strong artery walls.
rubric.description: Arteries have thick, muscular and elastic walls to withstand high blood pressure.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing the walls as thick and muscular or elastic.

rubric.why: Gives an additional structural or observable feature of arteries.
rubric.description: Their lumen is relatively narrow, and the rhythmic expansion of an artery can be felt as a pulse.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a narrow lumen or the pulse caused by arterial expansion.

rubric.why: States the usual oxygen content of arterial blood and its exception.
rubric.description: Arterial blood is usually oxygenated; the pulmonary artery is an exception.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying that arterial blood is usually oxygenated, with the pulmonary artery as an exception.

rubric.why: Explains how arteries distribute blood through the body.
rubric.description: Arteries branch into smaller arterioles that distribute blood to the tissues.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing the branching into arterioles or distribution to tissues.

modelAnswer: Arteries carry blood away from the heart to the body organs.
They have thick, muscular and elastic walls to withstand the high pressure of blood.
Their lumen is relatively narrow, and the rhythmic expansion of an artery can be felt as a pulse.
Arterial blood is usually oxygenated; the pulmonary artery is an exception.
Arteries branch into smaller arterioles that distribute blood to the tissues.
